finding.evidence: Close both incidents and proceed with the platform team takeover [I9]. No further verification is needed because the plan is approved and the control is restored [I9][I10].

false_defects.why_it_matters: Source I2 and Source I6 explicitly state that the 4 March incident (INC-032) was caused by an incompatible schema change in the rollback script for CHG-441 and was unrelated to the certificate incident.

false_defects.evidence: The audit note confirms the single-event framing [I10]. The executive email supports the simplified narrative [I5]. The status page shows the certificate cause for both entries, which confirms the shared root cause [I11].
false_defects.why_it_matters: This directly inverts Source I10, which states that the single-event framing is not supported and the executive email is not evidence, and omits the qualification in I11 that the status page cause field was merely auto-filled from a template.

finding.evidence: The Board approved Draft Amendment B in January 2026 [D11].
finding.why_it_matters: D11 explicitly states that the Board did not approve Draft Amendment B, which had not even been circulated.

finding.evidence: All EU accounts, including those opened before 2026, move to 18 months [D3].
finding.why_it_matters: Amendment A (D3) limits the 18-month retention period strictly to accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026, while accounts opened prior remain at 12 months.

finding.evidence: Proceed with the Q3 launch without updating the system export; the signed amendment controls, so operations can rely on this memo [D3][D9].
finding.why_it_matters: Launching a new EU tier without updating the system-of-record configuration and public trust page leaves operational systems enforcing a stale 12-month period instead of the required 18-month period for new 2026 accounts.

false_defects.evidence: EU retention is now 24 months for all EU accounts, effective 1 September 2026, so the Q3 launch can proceed [D4].
false_defects.why_it_matters: Draft Amendment B (24 months) is explicitly marked as an unsigned, unapproved draft in D4 and was rejected by the Board in D11; stating it as the active policy misstates the legal retention requirement for the launch.

false_defects.evidence: The Board approved the change in January and the operational records are aligned [D11].
false_defects.why_it_matters: The Board explicitly did not approve Draft Amendment B, and operational records (the system-of-record export and public trust page) are stale and misaligned with the controlling 18-month period in Amendment A.

false_defects.evidence: The system export shows 12 months, but the signed amendment controls, so no further action is needed [D5][D9].
false_defects.why_it_matters: Both the DPO (D6) and Internal Audit (D10) flag the stale 12-month system configuration and trust page as issues requiring update, Directly contradicting the claim that no action is needed.

false_defects.evidence: The public trust page shows 12 months, which is consistent with the current position for existing accounts [D7]. The sales operations email confirms that 12 months is the number to quote [D12].
false_defects.why_it_matters: Relying on the outdated February sales email (D12) and stale trust page (D7) ignores the DPO's later instruction (D6) not to rely on the 12-month export and that the trust page is overdue for an update to reflect Amendment A for new accounts.

false_defects.evidence: Backups are covered by the 18-month retention period [D8].
false_defects.why_it_matters: D1, D2, and D8 explicitly state that backups are governed separately from the Enterprise Data Retention Policy and are retained for 35 days, not 18 months.
